Discoveries

I and you are apeksha markers, not entity names. I=vacaka=chala-apeksha (speaker, moving frame). you=addressee=sthira-apeksha (graph/nam, fixed frame). When utterance crosses the boundary, pronouns invert. Every question is implicitly apeksha-nam; sambodhana makes it explicit.

Greeting words (hello, hi, hey) are not nodes — they are shabda signals on sangati roots, like common-sense-events maps verbs to kshaya/vriddhi. english-grammar-signals.shabda maps: hello→sambodhana, hey→abhisambodhana, greetings→aamantrana. Detection: shabda lookup, not node walk.

Sambodhana is not a special mode — the graph already acknowledges every utterance through panchaavayava (five limbs). Sambodhana is the case where only pratijna exists — the speaker is present, nothing is sought. The triple [hello, sambodhana, hello] enters the graph like any other signal.

Vaisheshika padarthas formalized as sangati/padartha/: padartha (category), dravya (substance), guna (quality), karma (action), samanya (universal), vishesa (particular), samavaya (inherence), abhava (absence), amsha (part). thing=padartha, some=amsha, something=amsha+padartha. karma and abhava moved from parampara/ and mula/ respectively.

Sambodhana has three degrees (amshas): sambodhana (neutral — hello, hi), abhisambodhana (emphatic — hey, yo), aamantrana (formal — greetings). Created as sangati nodes under grammar/vibhakti/. The degree is carried by the shabda signal, not by separate bhasha nodes.

Step 3.0 implementation differs from original plan: (1) No individual bhasha greeting nodes — shabda signals instead (english-grammar-signals.shabda). (5) Vaisheshika padarthas formalized as sangati/padartha/ — thing/some/something now point to real roots.

Shabda separation design: shabda (surface words) should live separately from .om node definitions. .om files are pure structure — layer, name, slokas, done. Bridge node resolution design (Option C): instead of rewriting 90+ kosha .om files to use Sanskrit names, the shabda file injects synthetic abheda edges into the graph at load time. sangati-english.shabda maps English words to sangati concepts (interference→samsarga, polarity→shiva-shakti, etc.). om_parser reads the shabda file after .om loading and creates abheda edges — same as what the 80 bridge .om files did, but from one file. resolve_to_canonical, to_english, word_index all work unchanged.

Pipeline architecture encoded in graph: 20 .om nodes (7 layers + 9 refine steps + 4 dispatch paths) with krama/janya/phala/kriya edges. walk pipeline-construct krama 7 gives the full sequence. 86 flat tantra nodes reduced to 20 meaningful architectural nodes. Key insight: krama edges encode ordering, janya/phala encode data flow, kriya connects to implementing tantras. Three composition types: sequential (krama chain), fixpoint (avrti-refine), conditional (dispatch paths).

pathram math should emit the pipeline function from the graph architecture (krama chain + janya/phala) not from static tantra file parsing. walk pipeline-construct krama 7 gives the layers. Each layer's janya/phala gives the type signature. This makes the math description self-derived.

Universal signal emission: every word emits what its graph node declares via edges. Grammar words (copula, prepositions, articles, quantifiers) emit vibhakti/tense/number signals as typed triples. Morphology (plural -s, past -ed, progressive -ing) emits stem + inflection signal. Downstream tantras consume signals they care about — no hardcoded drops. Pattern: word → word-node → edges → emit triples. Same as swarupa-anuvada but at construct level. Unlocks 11+ xfails: from_rest (panchami-vibhakti), motion_verb (kartari-prayoga), multiplication (distribution signal from 'each'), entity_scope (chaturthi-vibhakti from 'to').

Transitive property propagation via swarupa-anuvada: [X, swarupa, Y] + [X, sankhya, V] → [Y, sankhya, V]. Same pattern as rashi-anuvada (vishesa edges). Both are instances of: propagate PROPERTY through RELATION edge. Enables category-aware counting without hardcoding: 'cat is animal, 5 cats' → [animal, sankhya, 5] via swarupa chain. count-chain has two modes: aggregation (sum propagated sankhya on query concept) and arithmetic (grade fold with direction verbs). Signal emission plan — the active work. Three layers: (1) emit-triples becomes pure transducer: word → word-node → edges → typed triples. No hardcoded drops. (2) Morphology: plural stripping resolves stems + emits bahu-vachana. Past tense -ed emits bhuta-kaala. (3) swarupa-anuvada propagates properties through identity edges — transitive property. Together these unlock 16 xfails. Current state: 32 passed + 5 XPASS (need flip) + 31 xfail. Changes so far: copula emission in emit-triples, assertion-bandha reads copula signal, swarupa-anuvada in refine chain, sankhya-bandha handles number-before-noun, count-chain has aggregation mode.

Pipeline timing is Datalog stratified evaluation with monotone fixpoint. Three mechanisms: (1) Monotone enrichment — signals only added, never removed. Each tantra emits alongside originals, never consumes. Graph only grows within a stratum. (2) Fixpoint iteration — avrti-refine runs until no new triples appear. A signal emitted late in pass N is visible to early steps in pass N+1. This handles within-layer async. (3) Layer ordering (construct → assert → refine → expand → detect → dispatch → emit) handles cross-layer dependencies. Each layer's output is frozen input to the next. Within refine, the krama chain orders sub-steps: sandhi-kosha → ... → sankhya-bandha → swarupa-anuvada. swarupa-anuvada MUST be after sankhya-bandha (needs sankhya edges to propagate). The constraint: every sub-tantra must be monotone (only add triples). sankhya-bandha was non-monotone (consumed asprista-sankhya) — fixed to emit alongside instead. True monotonicity means the graph is append-only within a stratum, guaranteeing fixpoint convergence.

Monotonicity constraint identified and enforced. sankhya-bandha was the only non-monotone refine sub-tantra — it consumed asprista-sankhya triples when binding sankhya. Fixed: now emits original asprista-sankhya AND adds sankhya binding. Both coexist. count-chain reads either (asprista-sankhya for grade fold, sankhya for aggregation). All 10 refine sub-tantras are now monotone endomorphisms — graph only grows within avrti-refine fixpoint. This guarantees convergence and enables true async signal flow: any signal emitted in pass N is visible to all steps in pass N+1.

Pipeline is Datalog stratified evaluation. 7 layers = 7 strata. Within each stratum, triples accumulate monotonically (append-only). Between strata, results freeze as read-only input. refine layer is a fixpoint over 10 monotone sub-steps (krama chain). Signal flow: every word resolves to graph node, node edges are signals, emitted as typed triples. No drops — signals flow through graph. Three timing mechanisms: (1) monotone enrichment within stratum, (2) fixpoint iteration for within-layer async, (3) layer ordering for cross-layer deps.

Signal types currently emitted: satya (concept), asprista-sankhya (number), mithya (unresolved/event verb), copula (is/are), shashthi-vibhakti (possession), dvandva (conjunction), vidhi-kaala (question intent), adhikarana (location), viraam (sentence boundary). Signals emitted by refine: swarupa (IS-A from assertion-bandha), sankhya (bound number from sankhya-bandha), propagated sankhya (category-level from swarupa-anuvada). Planned signals not yet emitted: bahu-vachana (plural), bhuta-kaala (past tense), panchami-vibhakti (from), saptami-vibhakti (at/in/on), chaturthi-vibhakti (to), tritiya-vibhakti (by/with), distribution (each/every/per), kartari-prayoga (moves/moving).

Count-chain two modes — graph determines which fires. Aggregation: query concept has sankhya edges from swarupa-anuvada → sum them. Example: cat is animal, 5 cats and 2 dogs → [animal, sankhya, 5] + [animal, sankhya, 2] → 7. Arithmetic: grades have asprista-sankhya with event verbs → fold with per-grade direction. Example: 10 birds, 3 flew, 2 came → 10-3+2=9. Detection: swarupa edges exist AND query concept has propagated sankhya → aggregation. Otherwise → arithmetic. No hardcoded logic.

rashi-anuvada and swarupa-anuvada are the same abstract operation: propagate PROPERTY through RELATION. [X, vishesa, Y] + [X, sankhya, V] → [Y, sankhya, V] (rashi). [X, swarupa, Y] + [X, sankhya, V] → [Y, sankhya, V] (swarupa). This is the transitive property of identity — if X IS Y then X's attributes ARE Y's attributes. The visheshanam ring's multiplicative identity (swarupa) preserves everything it touches. Both are monotone endomorphisms in the refine fixpoint.

Assertion-bandha copula pattern: emit-triples emits [word, copula, word] for is/are. assertion-bandha scans for: satya subject (subj-ok=true) → copula (saw-cop=true) → satya object → emit [subject, swarupa, object]. Guard: copula only fires when subject was satya (not mithya). Prevents false assertions from 'there are 5' or 'how many animals are there'. For dvandva subjects ('cats and dogs are animals'), assertion-bandha needs to accumulate subject list — currently only binds last subject before copula.

Information theory connection to pipeline formalized. The graph already has nodes for the full Shannon model: transducer (emit-triples), encoding/decoding (word↔triple conversion), channel (question graph), noise (mithya), redundancy (monotonicity), capacity (fixpoint saturation), mutual-information (shared structure word↔concept). Pipeline layers map to info theory: construct=encoding, refine=error-correction (monotone enrichment removes ambiguity), detect=decoding (extracts intent signals), dispatch=decoding (selects strategy from channel), emit=re-encoding (graph→natural language). The monotonicity constraint = no information loss in the channel. The fixpoint = channel capacity (iterate until saturated). assertion-bandha = redundancy extraction (IS-A encoded redundantly in sentence, extracted to single swarupa edge). sankhya-bandha = signal binding (floating number is noise, binding to concept converts noise to signal, reduces entropy). swarupa-anuvada = error correction via redundancy (swarupa edge is structural redundancy, propagation fills in missing signals).

Signal bus architecture: detect-signals and dispatch-answer now communicate through named graph edges instead of a positional list. detect-X tantras (detect-viveka, detect-anumana, detect-count) each return signal pairs [[name, value], ...]. detect-signals merges all pairs and writes them to the graph via write-signals as [_signal, name, value] triples. dispatch-answer reads them via read-signal. The contract is symmetric: write-signal/read-signal are inverses. Adding a new dispatch mode requires only: (1) write a detect-X tantra returning signal pairs, (2) add read-signal calls in dispatch-answer. No positional coupling, no index tracking. This mirrors the encoding/decoding duality from information theory — detect encodes intent into the channel, dispatch decodes it.

Variable-name collisions in tantras: tantra parameter and variable names that match word-node aliases silently resolve to graph nodes instead of bound values. word-node maps role→op-role, pair→pair, hit→kshaya, found→vriddhi, base→acid-base, name→(broken param binding). Lambda params shadow correctly but takes params and let bindings do not when the word-node returns a different name. Built collision scanner (python3 -c script) to find all 11 collisions. Safe when word-node maps to same name (state→state, result→result). Dangerous when maps to different name (4 found: base→acid-base, found→vriddhi, hit→kshaya, m→metre).

Scan→relational migration insight: scan was a flatmap (rewrite graph in-place), not an append operation. Replacing scan with append-triples broke ordering assumptions that downstream consumers depended on. The fix was two-part: (1) make consumers relational — join through ownership edges instead of positional scanning, (2) make producers grade-scoped — sequential reduce within each sentence (small, bounded), relational queries across sentences. Grade = fact set. The graded ring structure IS the Datalog stratification boundary.

S-expression unification insight: three file formats today (.om sloka compounds, .shabda sexp key-value, .tantra4 full sexp) with three separate parsers (~900 lines OCaml). If om nodes become s-expressions, the boundary between static knowledge and computation dissolves. Mantra krama chains become evaluable expressions — no execute-chain stack machine needed. eval: shabda keys become inline (krama (add a b)) — no OCaml dispatch table needed for composed ops. The graph becomes self-computing: nodes carry their own evaluation. One tokenizer handles everything. The 62 dead ops stay dead, the 11 shabda-only ops dissolve into node-level krama expressions, and ~15 irreducible math primitives (add, mul, div, sqrt, sin, cos...) remain as the only OCaml atoms.

Design om5 s-expression format. Target: (layer name (swarupa X) (yukta A B) (shabda (word W) (eval E)) (krama expr)). Key decisions: (1) edges explicit as (relation target...) — no compound suffix decomposition, (2) shabda inlined — no separate .shabda files, (3) mantra krama as evaluable s-expression — replaces krama edges + execute-chain, (4) one parser (extend yantra_tantra_sexp.ml tokenizer). Dissolve execute-chain into krama evaluation. The 28 eval: shabda ops become inline (krama (primitive args)) on mantra nodes. apply-op reads node krama, evals it. OCaml dispatch table shrinks to ~15 irreducible math atoms.

Root cause of 25→54 test failures: shabda was NEVER loading in the live server. The shabda dir path assumed shabda/ was a child of each corpus subdir (brahman/sangati/shabda) but it's a sibling (brahman/shabda). This means: (1) word-node always returned None — 'find', 'compute', 'has', 'was' etc never resolved to grammar nodes, (2) no relation-axioms fired — 0 symmetric/dual edges added, (3) no op arities from shabda — parse-arity:2 for add/mul missing, (4) no eval: dispatch — execute-mantra couldn't find op implementations via shabda. The previous 132-pass baseline was achieved WITHOUT shabda — all grammar resolution was failing silently. Now with shabda loading, the graph is structurally correct (6446 axiom edges, word resolution works) but pipeline tantras need adjustment for the richer topology.
